causalModel.founding: Lilmoth stands on firm ground near shallow water. Large ships cannot dock at Lilmoth. Lighter crews carry goods ashore from the large ships. The lighter crews live aboard at permanent moorings. The moorings lie beside the lighter quay, on the way out to the anchorage.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The moorings are a permanent moored ground in sheltered water. The site lies about 460 m from Lilmoth. The site lies outside the tariff line.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The crews control the link between deep-water hulls and the city. The crews know what that link is worth.
causalModel.pressures: The council tried to license lightering. The attempt caused a two-week stoppage. Neither the council nor the crews want to repeat it.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: A dredged deep-water channel would end the flotilla. It would also end the city's hold on its own trade.

why.what: Five working hulls are moored bow-in along the south side of a timber pier. Four plank-ferry rafts are moored singly along its north side.
why.whyHere: Deep water lies close under the lagoon shore here. The site lies below the Lilmoth road.
why.whyNeighbours: The road to Lilmoth passes on the bank. The anchorage lies out on the open water.
why.playerPurpose: A traveller can hire a lighter to the anchorage here. Work, trade and a place to sleep are available at the flotilla.
why.microGeography: A flat bank lies at water level. Beyond the bank, 1.6 to 2.3 m of water lies under the hulls.

parcels.orientationWhy: Each hull is moored bow-in to the pier. The crew steps off the bow onto the pier.

why.what: The hull is a lighter crew's working boat. The hull is moored for good and is the home of its crew.
why.whyHere: The crews live where the work is. The work lies between the anchorage and the road.
why.whySpot: The hull lies in the row along the south side of the pier, where the water is deepest.
why.whyNeighbours: The hull is moored beside the other crew boats. The hulls lie as close as their shapes allow.
why.playerPurpose: The hull adds ambience. The crews who work the lighters live here.
why.microGeography: Deep water lies under the hull. The pier lies off the bow.

parcels.orientationWhy: The lighter lies off the end of the pier. Its bow points toward the anchorage.

why.what: The lighter carries passengers and cargo out to the anchorage.
why.whyHere: The end of the pier has the deepest water in the moorings.
why.whySpot: The lighter lies off the pier head, clear of the moored hulls.
why.whyNeighbours: The trade ship lies alongside the pier head beside the lighter.
why.playerPurpose: The lighter is the boat to the Lilmoth anchorage.

parcels.orientationWhy: The pier runs straight out east from the bank into deep water.

why.what: The street is a timber pier on piles, running from the bank out to the trade ship.
why.whyHere: The street is the only dry way from the bank out to the hulls.
why.whySpot: The pier starts on dry ground where the bank rises above the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The crew boats lie bow-in along its south side. The market rafts lie along its north side.
why.playerPurpose: The pier is the walk from the track to every boat, the market rafts and the lighter.
why.microGeography: The pier stands on piles over water 1 to 4 m deep.

parcels.orientationWhy: The trade ship lies alongside the pier head. Two stairs from the pier cross her rail to the waist.

why.what: The ship is the Alten Meerhleel trade ship. She is moored at the flotilla between runs. She has bunks to let and a purser's stores below.
why.whyHere: Large ships cannot reach the quays of Lilmoth through its shallow water. The lighters bring the cargo of the trade ship out to her here.
why.whySpot: She lies alongside the pier head, where the water is deep enough for her keel.
why.whyNeighbours: The crews' boats moor beside the trade ship. The lighters work her cargo to and from the city.
why.playerPurpose: The trade ship offers a bed, a trader and the boat to Alten Meerhleel.
why.microGeography: The deepest water lies off the pier head. She lies afloat there at low water.

playerPurpose.note: The boat to Alten Meerhleel boards here.
Spare bunks below decks, let to passengers.
The purser sells from the ship's stores.

parcels.orientationWhy: The stairs climb from the pier over the trade ship's rail. They go down to her waist.

why.what: The stairs are two short wooden stairs over the trade ship's rail.
why.whyHere: The ship's side has no opening. The way aboard climbs over the rail.
why.whySpot: The stairs stand amidships, beside the pier head.
why.whyNeighbours: The pier lies at the foot of the stairs. The waist and the cabin door lie beyond.
why.playerPurpose: The stairs are the way aboard the trade ship.
why.microGeography: The stairs cross the gap between the pier and the hull.

parcels.groundFitWhy: The stairs stand on the pier and the ship's deck. They never stand on the lagoon bed.

parcels.orientationWhy: The raft is moored with its long side to the pier, so one plank reaches it from the pier edge.

why.what: The raft is a plank ferry moored for good as a market stall.
why.whyHere: Lilmoth traders walk out along the pier to buy off the boats.
why.whySpot: The raft lies on the shallow south side of the pier, where the hulls cannot float.
why.whyNeighbours: Three other market rafts lie along the same side of the pier.
why.playerPurpose: The player can buy food and gear from the crews here.
why.microGeography: The raft rests in shallow water off the pier edge.

parcels.orientationWhy: The stage runs on the line of the Lilmoth track, so a walker steps off the track onto the planks without turning.

why.what: A short timber landing stage on piles across the reed shallows.
why.whyHere: The track from Lilmoth ends in ankle-deep marsh water. Carters will not drag barrows through mud.
why.whySpot: The stage starts where the track meets the water and ends on the firm bank beside the pier foot.
why.whyNeighbours: The main pier starts a few steps east of the stage's landward end.
why.playerPurpose: The dry way in from Lilmoth to the moorings.
why.microGeography: Reed shallows about a hand deep, with the bank rising to the south.

interiorClaim.why: 2 of 2 cells plugins link to kotm:argonia/tradeship/shipeectradeship01 (the base shell of composite:ship/eec-tradeship-with-door) pass; MurkmireTravelShipAltenMeerhleel is a barracks, 1 exterior load door; ties broken on the plugin's most-used cell (2 door links), then cell id

routes.why: The way in runs from the road along the stage and gangway to the street.

approaches.sequence: From the road the masts stand in a line over the lagoon. A plank stage runs out from the bank to the rafts.
approaches.wayfinding: Walkers go out along the stage and the gangway to the street.

approaches.sequence: Travellers coming east along the road see the trade ship's masts first over the low line of boats. The plank stage at the end of the bank comes next.
approaches.wayfinding: Walkers keep to the road until the stage. They then walk out along the stage and the gangway to the street.

networkTerminals.why: The track down from the Lilmoth road ends at the stage. The way out to the moorings starts at the stage.

combatSpaces.why: The pier is open water on both sides. The rafts moored off it are no wider. A fight on the pier ends in the lagoon.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The lore source is the catalogue record Lighter Flotilla (houseboat-flotilla, M2).
scaleGrounding.why: The crews live along one street on seventeen moored hulls, the lighter and a trade ship. These crews are named in the catalogue record.

candidates.why: The chosen site has deep water under the hulls. A dry bank below the road lies within reach of a plank stage.
The second candidate lies further west along the same shore, nearer the open lagoon.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The bank at the second candidate is wet to the road. A stage could start on dry ground at no point there.
